concepts.def: Bad News (1976) found systematic bias in TV news framing; selection and presentation favoured establishment views.
Direct effects model; criticised for assuming passive audience; supported by Bandura's Bobo doll work.
Blumler and Katz (1974): audiences actively use media for diversion, identity, relationships and surveillance.
Hall (1980): audiences make dominant, negotiated or oppositional readings of media texts.
Baudrillard (1981): hyperreality - media simulations replace reality; Gulf War 'did not take place' as media event.
Inequality in access and skills; Ofcom (2023) found 6% of UK adults are 'narrow users' lacking digital skills.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The Media — a core area of A-Level Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Media brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Media.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
